notes:
Rich describe on a 16 GB Mac
- Rich now fits a 16 GB Mac again: the 2B is a rung in the ladder, 448px is the
  floor no clip drops below, and the numbers the dial shows are the numbers it
  runs. One plan answers "does Rich fit, at what size, and what would free it".
- A long roll says what it will cost before it pays it, asks once, and reads
  1,200 frames per ffmpeg call instead of one call per window.
- Describe knobs that lied are gone: two deleted, one clamped, two now state
  the rule that actually runs. The Detail dial owns how often a clip is looked
  at and nothing else caps it.

Transcripts and words
- A Mac transcript carries word timings again: a clean CPU pass runs after the
  Apple-GPU decode, at the transcript's own Whisper size rather than capped at
  small. The word pass also runs on the card.
- Nothing records a clip as silent unless it actually listened.

Cameras and cards
- Cameras identify themselves now; the filename is only a hint. A RED clip is a
  folder, Canon's XML is not Sony's, and an unknown card still gets copied.
- Card recognition is two tiers: a bounded look on every poll, a full walk only
  when you ask. Cut Valet reads the timecode a camera actually stamped rather
  than the clock it guessed.

Progress you can read
- Every lane says what it is doing inside: eleven lanes got their sub-step
  writers, holds name which hold it is and what would clear it, skips name
  every reason, and failures name the clip.
- The Retry pill keeps its amber, and work that has stopped is described by
  surfaces that used to only know moving work.

Resolve and the MCP surface
- add_transition asks about the cut, because a dissolve is built from two
  clips' handles. Markers, batch indices, the gap a remove leaves, and project
  scope all behave.
- Document tools take project_id: a cut can be built for any project in the
  library, written from paths.
- An apply that put 83 clips in Resolve stops reporting that nothing was built,
  and a document-built timeline keeps a vertical project's shape.

Elsewhere
- Storage page: one drive list named by label, redrawn when the mount set
  changes.
- OpenRouter spend is priced per model. Nemotron writes metadata directly
  instead of spending its budget reasoning.
- Signals no longer sizes itself off hyperthreads or writes defaults when the
  passes it starved run out of time.
- The GPU gate covers the forward pass only; ffmpeg and HTTP moved outside it,
  and nothing slow runs in a timer slot any more.

# Changelog
added: Time of day sync, for lining up a whole day of cameras.
Tech stack, which scans this computer and tunes itself.
Ingest is a page, so several cards can land at once.
The assistant says what it knows, and every line has a switch.
